title: Rate Change and Pass-Through Notice Terms by Plan, Small Business Electricity Supply
content:
For each Small Business Electricity Supply plan, the terms below fix how far ahead a variable rate change must be notified, which billing cycles a new variable rate reaches, whether a fixed rate may carry a regulatory pass-through during the term, and how far ahead such a pass-through must be notified.

| Plan | Variable rate change notice (minimum calendar days before effective date) | Cycles a new variable rate applies to | Regulatory pass-through permitted during the term | Pass-through notice (minimum calendar days before effective date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Beacon Ridge Business Monthly Variable | 7 | cycles beginning on or after the effective date | no | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Business Fixed 12 | 7 | cycles beginning on or after the effective date | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Business Fixed 24 | 7 | cycles beginning on or after the effective date | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Business Fixed 36 | 7 | cycles beginning on or after the effective date | no | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Business Green 24 | 7 | cycles beginning on or after the effective date | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge Business Green 36 | 7 | cycles beginning on or after the effective date | no | 30 |

**Notes to the schedule**

1. The variable rate notice period is the minimum number of calendar days between the notice date of a business variable rate change and its effective date: 7 days on every plan.
2. A new variable rate applies to the billing cycles that begin on or after its effective date; a cycle that began before that date is not billed at that new rate.
3. The pass-through permission says whether a fixed rate may be adjusted during the term to pass through a change in law or regulation. It is "yes" on Beacon Ridge Business Fixed 12, Fixed 24 and Green 24, and "no" on Beacon Ridge Business Monthly Variable, Fixed 36 and Green 36.
4. The pass-through notice period is the minimum number of calendar days between the notice of a regulatory pass-through and its effective date: 30 days on every plan.

**Hypothetical illustration of note 2.** A new variable rate with an effective date of 1 June reaches a cycle running 3 June to 2 July, because that cycle begins after the effective date; a cycle running 20 May to 19 June began before the effective date and is not reached.
